This is one dissent recorded in a manifesto about sustaining human knowledge in the age of AI. Which fault line does it fall on?

Options:
- consent_or_payment: consent and payment mechanism: opt-in / levies / dues on existing text vs open training, pay at output, contracts for new work (Salib, Bratton, O'Reilly against the majority)
- model_in_loop: whether a model belongs in the checking loop or the room at all (Becker, Turkle)
- other: anything else

Text:

Open for reading is not open for training, so training should require author consent and retrieval should be favoured over pre-training.
raw: {"choice":"consent_or_payment","why":"The dissent is about consent as the mechanism governing use of existing text: \"training should require author consent.\" That is the opt-in position on the consent/payment fault line, set against open training. The preference for retrieval over pre-training follows from the same concern about how existing text gets used. It says nothing about whether a model belongs in the checking loop."}

parsed.why: The dissent is about consent as the mechanism governing use of existing text: "training should require author consent." That is the opt-in position on the consent/payment fault line, set against open training. The preference for retrieval over pre-training follows from the same concern about how existing text gets used. It says nothing about whether a model belongs in the checking loop.
